title: The 2+1 Baked Egg Formula: Build Dinner From Eggs, a Base, and a Bold Finish | Delixio
description: Use the 2+1 baked egg formula to turn eggs, a vegetable or bean base, and a bold finish into a flexible weeknight dinner.
h1: The 2+1 Baked Egg Formula: Build Dinner From Eggs, a Base, and a Bold Finish
intro: A carton of eggs can carry dinner when you give it a simple structure. The 2+1 formula keeps the decision small: choose **one base**, choose **one egg format**, then add **one bold finish**. Your pan, tray, or baking dish does the rest.

This guide gives you four ways to use that formula with vegetables, beans, bread, grains, or a sauce already waiting in the kitchen. Keep the quantities flexible. The useful question is: *what needs a dinner role tonight?*

sections.heading: The 2+1 formula at a glance

rows: Create a warm, sturdy bed for the eggs.
Roasted vegetables, white beans, spinach, mushrooms, tomato sauce, leftover grains
Pick the texture and equipment that suit the night.
Skillet eggs, tray eggs, baked eggs, soft scrambled eggs
Lemon, herbs, chilli crisp, feta, toasted breadcrumbs, olives, yoghurt, grated cheese

paragraphs_after: Start with a base that already has some moisture or can take a splash of water, stock, tomato sauce, or olive oil. Add the eggs near the end so they stay the centre of the plate.

sections.heading: 1. Tomato-and-bean baked eggs
paragraphs: Choose this route when you have a jar of tomato sauce, a tin of beans, and a baking dish or oven-safe skillet.
This format gives a can of beans a clear place in dinner and welcomes soft vegetables such as spinach, peppers, courgettes, or mushrooms.
steps: Warm tomato sauce with beans, onion, garlic, or any soft vegetables you have.
Make small spaces in the sauce and crack in the eggs.
Bake until the whites are set to your liking.
Finish with herbs, feta, chilli flakes, or toasted bread.

sections.heading: 2. The vegetable-tray egg dinner
paragraphs: Choose this route when the oven is free and you want one tray to do most of the work.
Good bases include peppers, onions, cherry tomatoes, broccoli, cauliflower, courgettes, or a handful of greens added near the end. Serve with bread, flatbreads, or leftover grains.
steps: Roast quick-cooking vegetables with olive oil and seasoning until they start to soften.
Make four small nests among the vegetables.
Add an egg to each nest and return the tray to the oven.
Finish with lemon, herbs, a spoon of yoghurt, or a shower of grated cheese.

sections.heading: 3. Skillet eggs over a savoury base
paragraphs: Choose this route when you want a fast stovetop dinner and a runny yolk sounds right.

Build a shallow base of mushrooms and greens, leftover roasted vegetables, beans, or a small amount of tomato sauce. Cover the skillet after adding the eggs so the whites cook gently. A lid, a splash of water, and a few minutes are enough.
Finish with something bright or salty: capers, olives, herbs, lemon zest, parmesan, or a spoonful of pesto. Use toast to scoop up the last bits from the pan.

sections.heading: 4. Crispy bread-and-egg baking dish
paragraphs: Choose this route when you have bread that wants a new job at dinner.

Tear bread into a small baking dish with sautéed vegetables, beans, or a little sauce. Add eggs on top, drizzle with olive oil, and bake until the bread has crisp edges and the eggs are cooked as you like them. A handful of cheese or breadcrumbs adds a good top layer.
This route works especially well with bread, roasted vegetables, greens, and leftover grains. The baking dish turns separate bits into a meal with a clear shape.

sections.heading: Match the formula to your evening

rows: Bread and a few loose ingredients

paragraphs_after: The formula stays useful when the details change. One night the base may be beans and tomatoes; another night it may be roasted vegetables and bread. The egg format gives the meal a direction before you start searching for a perfect recipe.

sections.heading: A short shopping-and-kitchen prompt
paragraphs: Keep two or three bold finishes around and dinner has more range: a lemon, a herb jar, chilli crisp, capers, feta, olives, or a hard cheese can move the same egg-and-vegetable base in different directions.
When you need another decision shortcut, read [[/guides/what-to-cook-tonight-when-you-have-ingredients-but-no-plan/|What to Cook Tonight When You Have Ingredients but No Plan]].

sections.heading: Make the formula your own
paragraphs: Pick one base, one egg format, and one finish. That is enough to start dinner with more momentum and less second-guessing.
